# LOOK RULINGS — the edge between autogenerated and composed

> The trench protocol applied to space. Drafts (generated rooms) are cheap and regenerable;
> rulings on the look are expensive and irreplaceable. Each pair below stages the same artifact
> cast twice — once as Palle composed it, once as the generator grew it (`grow_map.py --from-map`,
> seed 46). Palle rules in plain sentences: what reads composed, what reads generated, and *why*.
> Rulings are archived verbatim, numbered L-001…, and compile into the generators' contracts
> (staging DNA, rule-box knobs, gallery genomes). Nothing is applied without a ruling.
>
> Judging surface: `localhost:3003/look-pairs/` (chapter 1, primitives — 9 pairs).
> Thread: `the-edge` in doc/threads.json.

## How to rule

Look at a pair. Say what the composed one has that the grown one lacks (or the reverse —
sometimes the generator wins a point). Name the difference as a *property*, not a fix:
"the composed room leaves the hero a vacuum", "the grown room fills every cell",
"the composed wall knows where the door is going". One to three sentences per pair is enough.
Contradictions between rulings are content, not errors.
